lanes.summary: Diff (scripts-only: model_ladder cells producer + T-1 --cells wiring) is internally consistent with PMAT-3712/3715's producer/wiring scope, but the receipt's entire verification evidence table cites Rust/contracts tests and gates that touch none of the files actually in this diff, and never shows a run of the new check_ladder_cells_producer.sh or the changed check_release_models_t1.sh. Two secondary, lower-severity script issues (silent rungs-load failure swallowing, and thinking-budget sizing applied uniformly across modes) are also noted.

findings.file: receipt (section 4/6, 'Measured at the PR head' / 'Measured on this delta')
findings.claim: The receipt's entire verification evidence (cargo test -p aprender-contracts, cargo clippy on aprender-contracts, pv lint contracts, pv extract, the mutant kills on 'cell verdict'/'fresh()', check_complexity_ratchet.sh on shapes_gate.rs) is presented as evidence for this diff, but the diff under review contains zero Rust/contracts files — it touches only scripts/check_ladder_cells_producer.sh (new), scripts/lib/model_ladder_cells.py, scripts/lib/model_ladder_cells_produce.py (new), scripts/lib/model_ladder_cells_produce_cases/fake_apr.py (new), scripts/model_ladder.sh, scripts/release/models_t1.sh, and scripts/check_release_models_t1.sh. None of these files are mentioned in any 'Measured' table in the receipt.
findings.fix: Re-run and cite the actual self-tests for this diff — `bash scripts/check_ladder_cells_producer.sh` (the new producer's own case/mutant harness) and `bash scripts/check_release_models_t1.sh` (whose row count floor changed 37→40 and gained the cells-measured row/mutants) — and drop or clearly separate the unrelated aprender-contracts/Rust evidence, which belongs to a different PR.

findings.claim: `cells_for()` calls `J.load_rungs(rungs_doc, lambda _m: None)`, discarding every failure message `load_rungs` would normally report; if rungs.json is malformed or empty, the producer silently measures zero cells for that model instead of surfacing why, unlike the judge which prints the failure via its `out` callback.
findings.fix: Pass a real sink (e.g. append to a producer-visible log / return code) so a broken rungs file is reported by the producer itself rather than only showing up later as '0 cells' in the judge.

findings.claim: `target = min(tok, int(ctx) - a.max_tokens_thinking - 1) if ctx else tok` always subtracts the larger `max_tokens_thinking` budget when sizing the prompt for a rung, even for jobs in that same rung group whose mode is 'off' (smaller `max_tokens` budget) — so off-mode prompts near the declared context length are built smaller than they need to be, understating how close to the model's true declared limit the cell was actually exercised.
findings.fix: Compute `target` per (mode, budget) rather than once per rung group, or explicitly note in the receipt that off-mode declared-rung cells are deliberately under-sized (the comment only discusses the on-mode/judge conflict).

lanes.summary: The cells-producer wiring is otherwise consistent with PMAT-3712/3715 (owed_rungs refactor is behavior-preserving, --cells flag correctly threaded through models_t1.sh, tests/mutants added), but the new `--only` forwarding from model_ladder.sh into the cells producer silently reintroduces the exact "empty-universe vacuity" the file explicitly forbids for its own --only path.

findings.claim: `--only "$ONLY"` is forwarded from model_ladder.sh straight into `model_ladder_cells_produce.py measure`, but the two `--only` flags have incompatible semantics: model_ladder.sh's own $ONLY may be a bare rung id (e.g. "148k") or `inv:<file>`, validated against the union of rung ids + `inv:<file>` (scripts/model_ladder.sh:507-514,521-530); the producer's `--only` (scripts/lib/model_ladder_cells_produce.py:416) only ever filters by `it["file"]`/`"inv:"+it["file"]` — it has no rung-id branch at all.
findings.failure_scenario: `bash scripts/model_ladder.sh --cells --only 148k --host lambda` passes the top-level only_selected() check (148k is a legitimate rung id, scripts/model_ladder.sh:521-530), so the script proceeds and calls the cells producer's `measure --only 148k`. Since no inventory file is literally named "148k", cmd_measure's loop (model_ladder_cells_produce.py:413-418) skips every inventory row, and cmd_measure returns 0 with `cells: 0 row(s), 0 pass, 0 refused` written to cells.json and printed to cells.log — no error, no decline, exit 0. The ladder's own comment two lines above this exact call site (scripts/model_ladder.sh:517-520) names this precise failure mode as 'the worst possible instrument for the job --only exists to do,' yet the new --cells path has no equivalent guard: an operator using --only to reproduce/isolate one rung's cell failure (the documented purpose of --only, #3936) gets a receipt that silently claims zero cells for that host instead of measuring the requested rung, and cells_rc=0 so scripts/model_ladder.sh does not increment RED or flag anything wrong.
findings.fix: Either refuse to combine `--cells` with a rung-id-form `--only` (or pass an actual rung filter through to the producer), or have cmd_measure decline (non-zero exit, or at minimum a printed refusal) when the selection filters out every inventory row instead of writing an empty cells.json and returning 0.
